## Context / Problem
After S2, command identity/help and every handler grammar come from the registry/parser system, but real execution still traverses explicit intercept/dispatch ladders and policy frozensets. Leaving those selection authorities in parallel preserves the coordination defect RP-05 is intended to remove.

## Approach
Move core top-level execution to the selected registry route after the pre-operation help boundary. Resolve only the selected lazy handler reference and invoke it through a closed typed adapter-kind set matching existing call shapes. The router passes the original command remainder unchanged; the selected handler uses S2's shared argparse factory. The router must not parse command/nested options a second time.

Consume route metadata for:

- central best-effort mount eligibility;
- strict initialization `none`, `init_only`, or `full`, plus narrow pure selectors for genuinely conditional cases;
- position-independent confirmation/output extraction while preserving tokens after `--`;
- legacy output passthrough for `create`, `idea`, `transition`, `claim`, and `reopen`;
- exact handler adapter, argv, stdout/stderr, exit-code, and exception contracts.

Before cutover, compare registry-derived policies and selected handler/parser pairs to every existing set and arm. Any non-allowlisted delta fails shadow parity. Cut over one selection authority only after parity is exact; keep derived compatibility exports for S6 rollback.

This story covers core and bridge execution that does not change optional-capability posture. S4 owns selected optional mode/backend checks and may proceed from the same S2 contract without editing dispatch.

## Compatibility and Rollback
The positive rationale is a single validated selection/dispatch authority while preserving specialized parser-backed handlers. No signature introspection, middleware pipeline, eager parser-tree construction, or second parse is added. Rollback selects the derived compatibility exports; no event, ticket, bridge, or binding data changes.

## Testing
Use real CLI subprocess contracts rather than source greps. Extend mount/init, mutation confirmation, global output, bridge vocabulary, hidden alias, unknown, and exit-code suites. Add typed fake handlers for every adapter kind/selector. Include negative controls for tokens after `--`, malformed global flags, no-auto-mount commands, store-touching intercepts, handler exceptions, and a parser spy proving the selected handler parses exactly once while unrelated factories/handlers are not imported.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Every core canonical command and compatibility spelling resolves exactly one lazy handler through a closed adapter kind, and only the selected handler/parser modules are imported.
- [x] The top-level router preserves original remainder argv and the selected S2 factory parses it exactly once; no route-level option grammar exists.
- [x] Registry-derived mount/init behavior matches the pre-cutover census for every route, including no-auto-mount and conditional cases.
- [x] Confirmation, global output extraction, legacy JSON shapes, `--`, streams, exit codes, and exception propagation match existing behavioral tests.
- [x] Bridge compatibility spellings and hidden `bridge-status` execute through approved adapters while `purge-bridge` remains unknown.
- [x] Execution can switch back to derived compatibility exports without handler, generated-help, or persisted-data changes.
